claim: akasha says a day's span twice and the two do not agree. `getEsoDayWindow` answers `{ start: Date; end: Date }`, the stretch from one six-in-the-morning reset to the next; `DayWindow` in `health-samples-day` answers `{ from: string; to: string }` in ISO text, the stretch from when a day was recorded as opening to when the next day opened. One day string draws two different pairs of instants, and neither name says which stretch it hands back. Nothing derives either shape from the other, and reconciling the two onto one is unclaimed.

evidence:
Measured 2026-09-14.

`alan/harness/day/modules/eso-day/eso-day.module.code.ts:57` declares `getEsoDayWindow(dayStr): { start: Date; end: Date }`: the six-in-the-morning New York reset on that day to the same reset on the day after. A day string that is no day answers `{ start: new Date(0), end: new Date(0) }` rather than refusing.

`alan/harness/health-samples-day/modules/opening-window/opening-window.module.code.ts:13-16` declares `DayWindow` as `{ from: string; to: string }`, ISO text. `openingWindowIn` at `:151-161` fills it from the first sleep block recorded on the day's page to the first on the next day's, and refuses where either is unrecorded. `spannedWindowIn` at `:170-185` fills the same shape but falls back to six in the evening Mountain time the day before and to now or that evening, so two callers asking the same module about one day are handed two different stretches under one type.

Where the two meet: `alan/track/daily/modules/day-opening/day-opening.module.code.ts:20-25` (`openedDayWindow`) answers `spannedWindowIn` where that answers, and otherwise builds a `DayWindow` by hand out of `getEsoDayWindow` with `.toISOString()` on each end. That is the one place one shape is turned into the other, and it converts the type without converting the meaning: the reset-to-reset stretch is handed back under the name of the opening-to-opening one.

Who reads each: `agent/model/account/modules/pacing/model-account-pacing.module.code.ts:53` and `alan/harness/alan-readouts/modules/day-readout-watching/day-readout-watching.module.code.ts:298` take `getEsoDayWindow(day).end.getTime()`. `alan/harness/attributes/modules/totalling/attributes-totalling.module.code.ts:111-112`, `alan/harness/attributes/modules/reading/attributes-reading.module.code.ts:93`, `alan/harness/plants/modules/reading/plants-reading.module.code.ts:30` and `alan/track/daily/modules/nutrition-grams/nutrition-grams.module.code.ts:27` take `openedDayWindow`; `alan/harness/health-samples-day/modules/active-calories/active-calories.module.code.ts:30` takes `spannedWindow`. Nothing reads both, so no one caller has to reconcile them.

What lets it drift unseen: `new Date` and `Date.parse` take an ISO string and a millisecond count alike, and `.getTime()` on one side meets `.toISOString()` on the other, so a stretch handed across the seam typechecks whichever it is. No test judges that `openedDayWindow`'s fallback and `spannedWindowIn`'s fallback name the same instants, and they do not: one starts at six in the morning New York, the other at six in the evening Mountain.

Searching every `*.code.ts` for a type spanning a day answers these two and no third. Reconciling them touches `health-samples-day`, `day-opening` and every caller above, which is design work rather than a mend.
